name: Dragon's Mouth
summary: Dragon's Mouth refers to the treacherous geographic chasm and southwestern approach in the arid Badlands. While the region remains desolate and contested, the rugged passes around this valley form a natural choke point flanked by hostile beasts and encroaching ogres.

sections.title: A Rugged Choke Point
sections.body: Situated in the southwestern reaches of the Badlands, the area known as Dragon's Mouth marks a barren corridor cut through harsh red rock. In an unforgiving territory largely dominated by Horde scouts operating out of Kargath, wild drakes of the black dragonflight, and the brutal Dustbelcher ogres, this natural opening is a dangerous crossing for any traveler trying to survive the arid wastes.

faq.q: Is there an Alliance settlement at Dragon's Mouth?
faq.answer: No. The Badlands lack any fortified Alliance encampments, leaving travelers and explorers to rely on temporary camps or remote outpost networks like Morgan's Vigil far across the border in the Burning Steppes.

faq.q: What threats wander around this pass?
faq.answer: The surrounding flats and canyons are plagued by hostile Dustbelcher ogres, predatory buzzards, feral coyotes, and aggressive black whelps and drakes hunting across the red sands.

No single faction holds absolute control over the southwestern Badlands. While the Horde maintains an established staging post at Kargath to the northwest, the interior plains and rocky passes are dominated by wild beasts, rogue elementals, and territorial ogre clans.

angles.text: The Badlands offer virtually no friendly shelter for Alliance pioneers, making southern natural routes like Dragon's Mouth perilous terrain where travelers must constantly watch the ridges for Horde patrols and ravenous predators.
Warriors based out of Kargath monitor these remote southern corridors to ensure wild threats and intrusive Alliance scouts do not gain an unmonitored foothold in the region.
